Get accounts for all users from Pipedream Connect API and store them in MCP manager.
This endpoint fetches all user accounts and caches them for MCP server management.
List all Pipedream Connect accounts for a user.
List all stored accounts for all users (admin endpoint).

List all MCP servers and their tools for a specific user.
Returns servers that belong to the user based on their Pipedream accounts.

Unregister/remove an MCP server from a user's account.
Only allows removing servers that belong to the authenticated user.

List all supported OAuth providers.

Initiate OAuth authorization flow for a provider.

Steps:
1. Validate provider is supported
2. Generate OAuth state and PKCE parameters
3. Create PENDING connection in PostgreSQL
4. Store state in memcached for callback validation
5. Return OAuth authorization URL

Args:
    provider: Provider name (google, microsoft, etc.)
    request: Authorization request with user_id

Returns:
    JSON with auth_url to redirect user to

Handle OAuth callback from provider.

Steps:
1. Validate state parameter
2. Handle any OAuth errors
3. Exchange authorization code for tokens
4. Store encrypted credentials in PostgreSQL
5. Update connection status to CONNECTED
6. Redirect to success page

Args:
    provider: Provider name
    code: Authorization code from provider
    state: State parameter for validation
    error: Optional error from provider
    error_description: Optional error description

Returns:
    HTML success page or redirect

Check if user has completed OAuth for a provider.

This is used by frontend to determine if OAuth popup is needed.

Args:
    provider: Provider name (google, microsoft, etc.)
    user_id: User identifier

Returns:
    { "connected": true/false, "connection_id": "...", "created_at": "..." }

Disconnect a provider for a user.

Args:
    provider: Provider name
    user_id: User identifier

Returns:
    Success message

Get connection status for all providers for a user.

Args:
    user_id: User identifier

Returns:
    List of provider connection statuses

List all available MCP servers for a user, including both connected and unconnected.

This endpoint returns all MCP apps that are available through OAuth providers
(like Google Drive, Sheets, Docs) AND Pipedream apps, showing which ones are
connected and enabled. This allows the frontend to display "Connect" buttons
for unconnected services.

Args:
    user_id: User identifier
    account_id: Optional account identifier for LaunchDarkly targeting

Returns:
    Array of server objects with provider, app_id, connected status, enabled status, etc.

Retrieve a specific MCP service for a user.

This endpoint returns details for a single MCP service formatted the same way
as items in the list_provider_servers list. Useful for checking the status
of a specific service after enabling/disabling or for focused UI updates.

Args:
    provider: Provider name (google, microsoft, etc.)
    service: Service/app identifier (e.g., "drive", "google_drive", "sheets", etc.)
    user_id: User identifier

Returns:
    Single server object with provider, app_id, connected status, enabled status, etc.

Register MCP server for a provider after OAuth is complete.

This is the second step after OAuth authorization:
1. OAuth authorization completes → credentials stored
2. This endpoint → MCP server registered with agent runtime

Args:
    provider: Provider name (google, microsoft, etc.)
    request: Registration request with user_id

Returns:
    List of registered MCP servers in format expected by client

Disable a specific MCP service for a user.

This removes the service's tools from the agent context without
deleting OAuth tokens or unregistering the connection.

Args:
    provider: Provider name (google, microsoft, etc.)
    service: App ID or service name (google_sheets, sheets, etc.)
    user_id: User identifier

Returns:
    Full list of provider servers with updated enabled/disabled status

Re-enable a previously disabled MCP service.

This re-registers the MCP server and makes its tools available to the agent.

Args:
    provider: Provider name (google, microsoft, etc.)
    service: App ID or service name (google_sheets, sheets, etc.)
    user_id: User identifier

Returns:
    Full list of provider servers with updated enabled/disabled status

List all MCP servers registered for a user.

This endpoint returns all MCP servers that have been registered via OAuth,
including their connection status, tool counts, and metadata.

Args:
    user_id: User identifier

Returns:
    List of MCP server details with OAuth provider information

Get details for a specific MCP server.

Args:
    server_name: Name of the MCP server
    user_id: User identifier (for authorization)

Returns:
    Detailed server information including tools

Remove/unregister an MCP server.

This only removes the MCP server registration from memory.
The OAuth connection remains active in the database.
To fully disconnect, use DELETE /auth/providers/{provider}/disconnect

Args:
    server_name: Name of the MCP server to remove
    user_id: User identifier (for authorization)

Returns:
    Formatted list of remaining active servers (same format as GET /mcp/servers)

Refresh an MCP server's tools and update its token if needed.

This is useful when:
- Tools have been added/removed from the MCP server
- OAuth token has been refreshed
- Server needs to be re-initialized

Args:
    server_name: Name of the MCP server to refresh
    user_id: User identifier (for authorization)

Returns:
    Updated server information

Get MCP usage statistics for a user.

Args:
    user_id: User identifier

Returns:
    Statistics about MCP servers and tools

Return everything we have stored about ``user_id``.
Guaranteed explicit memory write used by "remember X" UI actions.

Delete one explicit phrase when a body is supplied, otherwise wipe all.

The legacy query-only shape ``DELETE /user_memory?user_id=...`` still
removes every stored record. A JSON body with ``phrase`` or ``key`` uses the
new explicit forget matcher instead.

List saved memory records by bucket for UI management.

Bucket names match the delete route's ``kind`` path parameter, so the UI
can pass an item's bucket name and key directly to ``DELETE /user_memory/{kind}/{key}``.
When ``conversationId`` is provided, the payload is emitted to the Socket.IO
room named by that conversation and the HTTP response is only an acknowledgement.
Guaranteed explicit memory delete used by "forget X" UI actions.

Merge ``patch`` into the existing profile record.

Creates the profile if none exists. Fields set to ``None`` on the patch
leave the existing value untouched; callers must send an explicit empty
list to clear a list field. Shares the per-user write lock with the
explicit API and ambient extractor so the single profile row is never
clobbered by a concurrent writer.

Update a collection memory record's strength by bucket and key.

Strength is only meaningful on collection buckets. Profile has no strength,
so callers should use ``PATCH /user_memory/profile`` for profile updates.
Disable or re-enable a saved memory entry by bucket and key.
Delete a single stored record by namespace ``kind`` and record ``key``.

List memories across all users in one bucket, sorted by strength desc.

Gated by an external API token whose row carries
``metadata.is_memories_admin = true``. Tokens without the metadata bit get
an empty list (with ``admin_enabled=false``) so unauthorized callers cannot
enumerate which tokens are admins.
